title: Palindrome check
instructorPromptText: Write a program that asks the user for a string, then prints True if it's a palindrome (ignoring case and non-letter characters) and False otherwise.

specGateDimensions.description: What counts as a 'non-letter character' to ignore — only punctuation and spaces, or also digits? For example, is '1A2A1' a palindrome?
specGateDimensions.rationale: The prompt says 'non-letter' but students often conflate this with 'non-alphanumeric'; committing in the spec prevents silent disagreement with test cases.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the program print for an empty string, or for a string that becomes empty after stripping non-letters (e.g. '123!@#')? What about a single character?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Degenerate inputs are the canonical missed cases in palindrome problems; the vacuous-truth question (is '' a palindrome?) has no default answer.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program normalize case only for the comparison, or also reflect normalized form in any output? Since only True/False is printed, confirm the original string is not echoed.
specGateDimensions.rationale: Forces the student to distinguish internal processing from output — a common source of scope confusion.

specGateDimensions.description: Will the cleaned string be compared to its reverse as a whole, or by walking inward from both ends? Either is valid but the spec should name one.
specGateDimensions.rationale: Unit 3 gives the student both slicing (s == s[::-1]) and index-based iteration; naming the approach before coding prevents a half-built hybrid.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Spec commits to ignoring non-letters, but code only lowercases and checks `s == s[::-1]`, leaving spaces and punctuation in the comparison so 'A man a plan a canal Panama' returns False
Spec says ignore non-letters (excluding digits), but code uses `c.isalnum()` and accidentally keeps digits
Plan describes building a cleaned list by iterating and appending letters; code uses a list comprehension or generator with ''.join(...) — coherent simplification
Plan describes comparing the cleaned string to its reverse via slicing; code uses a two-pointer while-loop walking inward — coherent alternative
Student reverses the string with `s.reverse()` (a list method) on a string and gets an AttributeError
Student prints 'True' or 'False' as strings via an if/else when they could just print the boolean expression, then misaligns a branch and prints the wrong literal
Case-normalizes one side of the comparison but not the other (e.g. compares `s.lower()` to `s[::-1]`)
